input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Deepen flagship 8 quick-pick-survey: replay the shipped selector and pooled ranking on real published rankings (PrefLib breakfast, T-shirt)

errors.fixed: the new test caught it; every slot is now indexed

errors.fixed: rewrote next: to a short state-plus-next item, with history pointing to the docs

doc_friction.issue: Default is the top allocate.py flagship, but flagship 1 (wall-framing-takeoff) had 265 commits in 7 days and every next: item says it needs real inputs from a builder; I took flagship 8 instead because a public real dataset existed for its 'real respondent' item.
run_workflow_locally.py --for-changes ran over the 120 s foreground timeout; worth listing it with the other long commands that need run_in_background.

--for-changes reported the sweep clean but did not run the workflow whose portfolio/router/validate.py step caught the flagships.yaml next: length cap on GitHub; a touched portfolio/flagships.yaml should select it.
Says to 'rewrite that venture's next:', but not that validate.py caps it at 2000 characters; the quick-pick entry was already at ~2000, so any append fails.

deviations.why: Took flagship 8 (quick-pick-survey), not the top row: flagship 1 is saturated and its items need real builder inputs, while flagship 8 had an outside-data item that public real data could answer.
deviations.did: Measured the survey on PrefLib real rankings
deviations.result: Landed a measurement and an opt-in rule; it changed the flagship's next: to a concrete, testable item

deviations.why: `npm run verify` includes `next build`, which this change does not touch (lib + script + docs only).
deviations.did: Ran typecheck, lint and the fast vitest suite (316 tests)

goal: Depth over calculators: a real-data measurement of a flagship's core method
notes: Data: PrefLib 00035 breakfast and 00012 shirt, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com and pinned by sha256, not committed (PrefLib-Data is GPL-3.0). SUSHI was rejected because its licence is research-only with no redistribution. Verification: npm run typecheck, npm run lint and vitest.fast (36 files, 316 tests) all pass. The new difference-rule test fails when the rule is ignored. Eval: 4 runs x 200 seeds, about 30 s each. Out-of-sample scoring was added after the first pass showed that scoring against the whole panel flatters large samples of a small panel.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: data sourcing and licence check, eval harness, 4 parameter sweeps, write-up

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
